identity.title: Vertical CO surfaces as a probe for protoplanetary disk mass and carbon depletion

paper_type_evidence.quote: we benchmark our results with ALMA observations of CO emission from nineteen disks
The results shown in this paper are based on an extensive grid of models run with the thermochemical code DALI

question.value: How the vertical extent of the 12CO 2-1 emission surface in protoplanetary disks depends on stellar and disk parameters, especially total disk mass and volatile carbon depletion

evidence.quote: This project aims to relate the vertical extent of protoplanetary disks as traced by $^{12}$CO $2-1$ to key stellar and physical parameters.
The CO emission surface location is primarily determined by the disk mass ($M_d$) and the level of volatile carbon depletion.
This work focuses on the protoplanetary disk properties that affect the vertical structure as traced by bright $^{12}$CO $2-1$ emission.

pi_or_archival_as_stated.value: Archival 12CO 2-1 data cubes of 19 mid-inclination disks, with emission surfaces taken from previous works

evidence.quote: We present a $z/r-$Disk mass relation for both T Tauri and Herbig disk systems and apply it to a sample of archival protoplanetary disk observations.
This sample has been constructed from mid-inclination disks with available $^{12}$CO $2-1$ data cubes from which the surfaces have been extracted and published in previous works

referee_caveats_inferred: Mass and carbon depletion are degenerate; the depletion is only fixed by assuming a dust-based gas-to-dust ratio of 100 as truth, so depletion is partly circular
Dust-based masses are uncertain by large factors (opacity, temperature, scattering), which feed directly into the inferred depletion
Only two template stars; stellar-mass dependence within each class is not explored beyond luminosity and temperature
Observed z/r values come from heterogeneous surface extractions (ALFAHOR vs DISKSURF), resolutions and data sets, with uncertainties from radial-bin scatter only
Model z/r is defined from the tau=1 surface, while the observed one is from channel-map emission maxima; the systematic offset between them is not quantified in this paper
No uncertainty propagation for the literature mass and depletion choices; 'preferred depletion' is judged by eye at 0, 10 or 100
